newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Turnover lower, prices higher on Bucharest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Turnover lower, prices higher on Bucharest bourse.

text.p: Turnover on the Bucharest stock exchange dropped by some 1.0 billion lei to 1.2 billion on Thursday, but traders said it was nonetheless high compared to last year's levels.
The only two stocks listed on the first tier -- Azomures SA fertiliser maker and chemical plant Oltchim SA -- took 89 percent of the session's record 1,574 trades.
"Trading in the two heavyweights stayed strong, with demand slightly higher than supply pushing prices up," a broker said.
Azomures had 915 trades on turnover of some 658 million lei and closed 20 lei higher at 1,620.
Oltchim had a turnover of 386.2 million lei and closed 130 lei stronger at 1,650.
"The two will continue to give the tone of the market for quite a large number of sessions ahead, at least till another company joins trading on the first tier," a trader said.
Demand outrunning supply sent most prices up. Fifteen stocks drifted higher, two fell, three marked time and one -- newcomer Cercom SA building materials company -- had no trade.
Two independent indices climbed to year highs, following a trend which has started early this year.
The day's second newcomer, Armatura SA plumbing equipment producer, closed at 500 lei, flat on its opening quote.
"For the newcomers, their first day of trading was a day of probing," another trader said. "They will eventually appeal to investors because they are privately held."
The bulk of the 22 stocks traded on the Bucharest exchange are state-run companies.
Two unofficial indices -- the VAB and the BIG -- rose to year highs, going up by 6.1 and respectively 6.14 percent from the previous session.
